rawData.Description: The previous transactions of the card are recorded in the OTB (Open to Buy), these are added to the CH balance upon update to prevent overlimit. These transactions are removed from the OTB table If these transactions are settled by VISA.&
rawData.Identified Root Cause: Unauthorized or Improper Access: Access to systems, areas, or data without valid authority, including misuse of credentials.
rawData.Identified Root cause of the Problem: The problem roots from the lack of access of workstation .89 on the Batch Systems. This was the impact during the migration has the access from Binondo to VITRO.
rawData.Findings:
The previous transactions of the card are recorded in the OTB (Open to Buy), these are added to the CH balance  upon update to prevent overlimit.  These transactions are removed from the OTB table If these transactions are settled by VISA.   In this case, some of the transactions were included in the CH balance temporarily , even if these were posted to VISA causing the additional amount added to the CH balance. 

Upon checking, the workstation 111.89 doesn't have access on Batch Systems. This caused the OTB matching not to properly match the details between the transactions in Batch and Auth. This caused the incorrect  balances between Batch & Auth

affected records were:
ONG, 
4617-xxxx-xxxx-5043
BARIA, 
4617-xxxx-xxxx-7035
PASAGUI, 
4617-xxxx-xxxx-1042
SARNO,
4617-xxxx-xxxx-4017
GO, 
4617-xxxx-xxxx-5013
rawData.Resolution:: The respective network access has been provided  and it has since correctly reflect the balances on the workstation 111.89 since 10/15/2026. Other application and workstations have been check for the connections.
rawData.Lessons Learned: Need to thoroughly check the access workstations before the migration activity
rawData.Subject: CardSuite BATCH and AUTH Balance Disparity

routedIncidents.description: Our air conditioner has a water leak.

rawData.Location of the Incident:: POS Repair Department 7th floor Binondo Manila
rawData.Description: Our air conditioner has a water leak.
rawData.Identified Root Cause: Equipment Failure: Breakdown or malfunction of machinery or equipment.
rawData.Identified Root cause of the Problem: Accumulated dirt and slime inside the drain line blocked the water flow, causing the cooling coils to overflow from the indoor drain pan.
rawData.Findings: Drain line clogged with algae, and dust causing condensation to back up and overflow.
rawData.Resolution:: Cleared and flushed the drain line using high-pressure water, thoroughly cleaned the indoor unit drain pan
rawData.Lessons Learned: chemical wash and drain flushing schedule for all indoor ACU units
rawData.Subject: Hardware Issue
rawData.Closing Comments: The ticket is now officially closed. The requester can reopen this ticket if the leak recurs.

routedIncidents.description: The previous transactions of the card are recorded in the OTB (Open to Buy), these are added to the CH balance upon update to prevent overlimit. These transactions are removed from the OTB table If these transactions are settled by VISA.&

rawData.Description: The previous transactions of the card are recorded in the OTB (Open to Buy), these are added to the CH balance upon update to prevent overlimit. These transactions are removed from the OTB table If these transactions are settled by VISA.&
rawData.Identified Root Cause: Unauthorized or Improper Access: Access to systems, areas, or data without valid authority, including misuse of credentials.
rawData.Identified Root cause of the Problem: The problem roots from the lack of access of workstation .89 on the Batch Systems. This was the impact during the migration has the access from Binondo to VITRO.
rawData.Findings:
The previous transactions of the card are recorded in the OTB (Open to Buy), these are added to the CH balance  upon update to prevent overlimit.  These transactions are removed from the OTB table If these transactions are settled by VISA.   In this case, some of the transactions were included in the CH balance temporarily , even if these were posted to VISA causing the additional amount added to the CH balance. 

Upon checking, the workstation 111.89 doesn't have access on Batch Systems. This caused the OTB matching not to properly match the details between the transactions in Batch and Auth. This caused the incorrect  balances between Batch & Auth

affected records were:
ONG, 
4617-xxxx-xxxx-5043
BARIA, 
4617-xxxx-xxxx-7035
PASAGUI, 
4617-xxxx-xxxx-1042
SARNO,
4617-xxxx-xxxx-4017
GO, 
4617-xxxx-xxxx-5013
rawData.Resolution:: The respective network access has been provided  and it has since correctly reflect the balances on the workstation 111.89 since 10/15/2026. Other application and workstations have been check for the connections.
rawData.Lessons Learned: Need to thoroughly check the access workstations before the migration activity
rawData.Subject: CardSuite BATCH and AUTH Balance Disparity

routedIncidents.description: CCTV monitoring at 209.205 connected but cameras were loading only

rawData.Description: CCTV monitoring at 209.205 connected but cameras were loading only
rawData.Identified Root Cause: Software Issues: Bugs, glitches, or compatibility problems in software systems.
rawData.Findings: Detected the Vivoek interface all camera are loading
rawData.Lessons Learned:
1. Check Connections: Ensure that all cables are securely connected. This includes power cables, HDMI or VGA cables, and any network connections. A loose connection can often be the culprit behind a lack of display.

2. Power Cycle the Device: Sometimes, simply restarting the NVR can resolve display issues. Unplug the device, wait for a few seconds, and then plug it back in.

3. Monitor Compatibility: Verify that the monitor or display being used is compatible with the NVR. Check the resolution settings and ensure the monitor is functioning properly with other devices.
